acceptance: trunk.yml and test.yml use the same duration file, or the omission is recorded as a decision
A scheduled or documented refresh of the duration file exists
Worst shard within about 10% of the mean over at least 10 PR runs
context: 2026-10-21: remaining part (1) for trunk.yml is delivered by trunk-coverage-workflow-map-v2-20261021, which returns trunk medium-test to uninstrumented duration-weighted shards. test.yml and the refresh remain here.
description: DONE in #3218 (merged b38ed2385): the pull-request workflow (ci.yml) now assigns medium tests to the 4 shards longest-first using tests/fixtures/medium_shard_durations.json (988 tests of at least 0.25 s plus a 0.0278 s default for the rest, built from CI run 39538637499), and each shard writes a junit report. Measured on CI, slowest shard before 1020 s (others 632, 609, 426); after 717 s and 726 s on two runs (others 527-608 s), a drop of about 300 s (30%). The predicted balance from the real per-test timings was 843/848/843/844 s (max/mean 1.004), but the measured shards are still uneven (527 to 726 s) because the prediction ignores per-shard fixed cost and test interaction on the runner; that gap was not investigated. REMAINING: (1) trunk.yml and test.yml still use round-robin; (2) the duration file will drift as tests change and nothing regenerates it; _project/scripts/update_test_durations.py --min-seconds 0.25 rebuilds it from shard junit reports; (3) investigate why measured shard times stay uneven (shard 0 still slowest by about 120 s); (4) tests added since the file was built are weighted at the default.
